items.title: Loren Schoenberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2019
items.q: the band on that record was Dick Katz, Howard Alden

ctx.x: players and — it was about fifty percent young and fifty percent older, of course much — the old guys were younger than I am now. And so the band started to cotton. And in the meantime Goodman asked me to come back because this woman I had mentioned before, Muriel Zuckerman, who had been his Girl Friday, she quit, and he said, “Can you come in and just, until I find someone, answer the phones or just help with something?” So I started doing that, and then eventually when he found out that I knew musicians and I…

Later on, as the band got professional and as I started to make a living in music, all those guys, I mean I paid. I paid for arrangements. I paid arrangers and I paid — but at this time there was nothing there. So John Hammond and a few other things and things started, and next thing you know we’re going to make a record. So we made a record for a guy named Jerry Valburn who issued a lot of radio broadcasts with like a big jazz collector who had his own little labels. And he had a label and he started recording…

he had a Mercedes. So on some weekends I would actually drive Benny up with Carol to their house, like the chauffeur, drive them up to Stamford, leave them, then I would drive his car back and park it in his garage. And I mean I had never driven a Mercedes Benz but that’s another story. Drive it back, park it in his garage, and somehow they would get back on Sunday. Well one time I went up there and one time I went up there and he invited me for lunch and one time he said let’s go swimming, he had a swimming…
